title: SPECRUN: The Danger of Speculative Runahead Execution in Processors
problem: Runahead execution, a processor performance optimization technique, is vulnerable to transient execution attacks that exploit unresolved branch predictions during speculative execution. These attacks can generate speculative instructions beyond the reorder buffer size limit, enabling secret leakage from victim processes.
motivation: Runahead execution is an important microarchitectural optimization technique, but security vulnerabilities in such optimizations must be identified and addressed before deployment.
method: The SPECRUN attack exploits unresolved branch predictions during runahead execution to generate transient instructions that exceed normal reorder buffer limitations. By inducing speculative execution along mispredicted branches, attackers create a larger window of unresolved instructions that can leak sensitive data. The paper demonstrates proof-of-concept secret extraction and proposes a secure runahead execution scheme as mitigation.
key_novelty: First transient execution attack specifically targeting runahead execution that eliminates reorder buffer size constraints on exploitable transient instruction windows.
contributions: Introduces SPECRUN, the first transient execution attack on runahead execution
Demonstrates bypassing of reorder buffer size limitations on transient instructions
Provides proof-of-concept attack demonstrating secret leakage from victim processes
Proposes secure runahead execution design to mitigate the vulnerability

metrics.other: demonstrates successful secret leakage from victim process via transient execution side-channel

baselines: baseline runahead execution without security measures
limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: microarchitecture security vulnerability in speculative execution
